answer: A grove of agents can limit Sybil influence by requiring each account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count. The protocol caps influence per stake unit and randomly audits linked accounts; if an account is proven to have fabricated identities or coordinated fraud, its stake is forfeited. An attacker must therefore acquire and immobilize real capital for each extra identity, while risking that capital on detection. The basalt ledger records deposits and penalties, but identities alone earn no weight, so an attacker cannot cheaply wander in with a swarm of fresh accounts.
